exam.title: Midterm Exam
exam.description: CSE120 Midterm covering processes, threads, and synchronization
exam.instructions: Select the best answer for each question. You have 90 minutes to complete this exam.

A.rationale: Correct! A process is an instance of a program that is being executed.

B.rationale: Incorrect. A compiled binary is just the executable file, not a running instance.

C.rationale: Incorrect. A thread is a unit of execution within a process.

D.rationale: Incorrect. A system call is a request to the operating system kernel.

questions.explanation: A process represents a program in execution, including the program code, current activity, and allocated resources.

questions.question_text: Which scheduling algorithm can lead to starvation?

A.rationale: Incorrect. Round Robin ensures all processes get CPU time periodically.

B.rationale: Incorrect. FCFS serves processes in order, preventing starvation.

C.rationale: Correct! Low-priority processes may never execute if high-priority processes keep arriving.

D.rationale: Partially correct, but priority scheduling is the classic example.

questions.explanation: Priority scheduling can cause starvation when low-priority processes are continually preempted by higher-priority ones.
